title: Customer Care Policy: First-Incident Courtesy for Cleaning and Damage Fees
content:
A disputed Cleaning and Damage Fees charge at a level whose first-incident courtesy eligibility is "Yes" may be reversed once as a first-incident courtesy, even though the evidence meets the standard. The courtesy applies only when the rider has no other charged, disputed or upheld assessment with a charge date in the courtesy lookback, counted across all of the rider's assessments. The courtesy refund carries the refund reason courtesy first incident, and the driver keeps the payout.

## The lookback

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Length | the level's courtesy lookback, 365 calendar days |
| Where it ends | on the day before the trip of the assessment in question |
| What is counted | the rider's other assessments, on any trip, whose charge date falls in the window and whose status is charged, disputed or upheld |
| Condition for the courtesy | that count is zero |
| Authority | the system record of the rider's assessments, tied to the rider |

## Truth table

| Level eligible for the courtesy | Other charged, disputed or upheld assessment with a charge date in the lookback | Courtesy |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | none | may be granted, once |
| Yes | one or more | does not apply |
| No | any | not available at that level |

## Boundary illustration (hypothetical dates)

The trip of the disputed assessment took place on 15 June 2026, so the lookback runs from 15 June 2025 through 14 June 2026.

- Another assessment against the same rider was charged on 14 June 2025 and was upheld. Its charge date is outside the lookback, so it does not count.
- Another assessment charged on 15 June 2025 and still charged is inside the lookback, so the courtesy does not apply.
- Another assessment charged inside the lookback whose fee was later reversed holds the status reversed and is not counted.
